d:
On pages 22 and 23, you may notice that some Japanese characters in the speech bubbles have been left untranslated. When an entire page of onomatopoeia has a consistent style and part of it is divided by speech bubbles, as shown in the images, placing the translation either inside or outside the bubbles would be far from elegant. In the end, I decided not to translate them, because I felt that leaving the foreign scripts intact could, to some extent, help convey the striking effect of moans and SFX blending together in the original text. Trust me, I'm not just making excuses to cut corners. Cleaning and redrawing the rest of the bubbles was actually a hundred times more work.

If this sweet story helped you relieve some stress, please consider buying the artist a coffee.
